_comment: Spelling rules the project owner has asked for, waiting for a second Zomi reviewer. NOT adopted and never applied: a rule is adopted only when two different reviewers agree (docs/ZOMI_STANDARD_FORM.md), and then moves to standard.json with an ID. `zolai_standard.py preview` shows what these would change. The SZSF converter and `apply` do not read this file, so no master file carries these changes until a rule is adopted.

proposals.owner_words: I want to use as the Bible uh hi
proposals.reason: The project owner chose the Bibles' spelling, two words, because 'uh' marks the plural and 'hi' is the verb (owner_example). This also follows the Standard Form tie-break (common published usage first).

evidence.corpus: uhi: 32,520 words in 31,247 pairs; uhhi: 473 words in 464 pairs (language database v2, 2026-11-13)
evidence.tedim_bibles: 'uh hi' as two words 21,496 times; 'uhi' and 'uhhi' 0 times (TDB and TB77)
evidence.dictionary: 'uhi' and 'uhhi' 0 times in the 50K Translation Master
evidence.context: In the corpus 'uhi' appears mostly in pairs about 'they', 'their', 'people', 'each', 'both' (plural subjects), the same use as 'uh hi'
evidence.related: rule check uh-hi lists 'uh hi' and 'uhhi' (the Zolai Standard Format writes uhhi); 'uh hiam' / 'uhhiam' is the same question for the question form and is not part of this proposal
evidence.corpus_two_word_form: 'uh hi' as two words is already the main spelling in the corpus: 142,392 times, against 32,520 for 'uhi' and 473 for 'uhhi'

proposals.owner_reason: uh is plural and hi is verb, for example: they will go. Amaute pai ding uh hi.

proposals.owner_words: if you see "thil", replace with "na", etc
proposals.reason: The project owner asked for 'thil' to be written 'na'.

evidence.corpus: thil: 14,379 words in 14,140 pairs (language database v2, 2026-11-13)
evidence.tedim_bibles: 'thil' 0 times; 'na' 9,314 times (it also means other things, see caution)
evidence.other_chin_bibles: 'thil' appears in the Falam Bible (1,620) and the Hakha Bible (2,230), so it may be a word of another Chin language
evidence.context: In the corpus 'thil' appears mostly in pairs about 'things', 'something', 'everything', 'happen'
evidence.tedim_bible_for_things: Aligned with the English Bible, the Tedim word most tied to 'thing(s)' is 'nate' ('na' with the plural 'te'): 112 of 1,504 verses, 6.9 times the usual rate
evidence.caution: 'na' is also a very common word with other meanings in the Tedim Bibles, so the sentences need a Zomi reviewer's check in context. A reviewer may prefer mode 'flag' first, which lists each match and changes nothing.

suggested_not_decided.note: Follows from P-002 ('thil' + 'te' becomes 'na' + 'te'), and 'nate' is the Tedim Bible's word for 'things'. The owner has not decided it: 'thilte' appears 1,623 times in the corpus and in the Hakha Bible only.
suggested_not_decided.needs: the project owner's decision, then a second reviewer

suggested_not_decided.note: The question form, by the same reasoning as P-001 ('uh' plural, 'hiam' the question verb). 'uh hiam' as two words is the main form in the corpus (10,911 times); 'uhiam' appears 947 times and 'uhhiam' 9 times. It is already a pair in the rule check uh-hi. The owner has not decided it.
suggested_not_decided.needs: the project owner's decision, then a second reviewer
